android.notes:
**Record your analysis.** Open a clip, mark it up, talk over it, and send the session instead of a still. One button in the app bar starts a take. It begins paused, so nothing is captured until you press play, and the controls stay in the bar's own band the whole time: a mic that starts shut and opens when you want to be heard, a coach view that puts your face in a corner bubble you can drag and resize, and a stop. Before you start, the sheet tells you how much room your phone has left in minutes, and asks one question about the clip's own sound — mute it, duck it under your voice, or talk over it. The controls themselves are drawn on that sheet, so you know what you are about to be handed.

**Stop opens an editor, not a save dialog.** The take fills the screen and you trim it with the loop cues you already know: drag to seek, hold to play the kept part, tap a handle and walk it a frame at a time with the arrows, `[` and `]` to mark where you are. A four-edge frame crops the picture, with 9:16, 16:9, 1:1 and 4:5 to snap to and a button that cuts the app's own bars off the top and bottom. Nothing is written until you save, and backing out asks first, because a take is minutes of your own voice.

**Save and share at the speed you were watching.** Whenever the clip is running at something other than 1×, the save and share screens offer to keep it there. It is a retime rather than a re-encode, so slow motion saves as fast and as cleanly as an ordinary cut. A retimed clip is silent — the sheet says so — because a copied soundtrack cannot honestly be stretched.

**The bottom bar stops moving.** Arming a drawing tool used to shove the zoom, the mirror and the speed sideways; now nothing moves. Compare with only one video loaded keeps the full row of controls instead of falling back to bare step arrows, a clip beside a photo gets its own mute, and the speed sits ahead of the play arrows everywhere a phone row carries both.

**Also, since 0.5.0:** mirror a video for a facing-camera comparison, zoom into a stretch of the scrub bar, a reworked compare layout, and sharing an InForm file so the person you send it to gets your arrows and angles as arrows and angles rather than burned into the picture.
